name: Application.start
syntax: public class App extends Application { public void start(Stage stage) }
desc: The entry point of a JavaFX program. launch builds the FX thread and calls start with the primary stage.

name: FXMLLoader
desc: Builds the scene graph from an FXML file. load returns the root node and getController returns the controller instance.

name: Scene
desc: Holds the scene graph that a stage displays. Width and height are the window content size, not the screen size.

name: Stage title and close
desc: The stage is the top level window. Set the title, a minimum size, and a close handler before showing it.

name: Button setOnAction
desc: Attaches a handler to a button click. The handler runs on the JavaFX application thread, so keep it short.

name: Label
desc: Shows read only text. setWrapText and setMaxWidth keep long names inside the layout.

name: TextField
desc: A single line text input. getText returns an empty string when the field is untouched, never null.

name: TextArea
desc: A multi line text box. appendText adds to the end and keeps the caret at the bottom, which suits log output.

name: ComboBox
desc: A drop down list with one selected value. It can be editable, which turns it into a combo of list and text field.

name: ListView
desc: A scrollable list of items. Back it with an ObservableList so the view follows every change.

name: TableView
desc: A table bound to a list of row objects. Columns decide what is shown, the items hold the data.

name: TableColumn cellValueFactory
desc: Tells a column how to read a value from a row. The lambda runs for every visible cell, so keep it cheap.

name: VBox
desc: Stacks children vertically. The spacing constructor argument is the gap in pixels between them.

name: HBox
desc: Places children side by side. Hgrow decides which child absorbs the extra width.

name: GridPane
desc: Arranges nodes in rows and columns with explicit cell coordinates. Column constraints control the widths.

name: BorderPane
desc: Splits the window into top, left, right, bottom, and center. The center region grows, the others keep their size.

name: Alert
desc: A modal dialog for messages and confirmations. showAndWait blocks until the user picks a button.

name: Platform.runLater
desc: Schedules a task on the JavaFX application thread. UI changes from a worker thread must go through it.

name: Task
desc: Runs background work with success, failure, and progress callbacks that already run on the FX thread.
body:
## Task against Platform.runLater

`Platform.runLater` moves one update to the FX thread. `Task` also returns a result and reports failure, so the success path and the error path stay separate.

## Rules

- Only `call` runs on the background thread. Do not touch controls there.
- `setOnSucceeded`, `setOnFailed`, and `updateMessage` run on the FX thread.
- Call `setOnCancelled` when a cancel button exists, otherwise the worker keeps running.
- One `Task` runs once. For repeated work use `Service` and call `restart`.

name: FXML controller with @FXML
desc: Connects an FXML file to a Java class. fx:id fields are injected and onAction="#method" calls the annotated method.
body:
## How the wiring works

The loader reads `fx:controller`, creates that class, and matches every `fx:id` attribute to a field of the same name. A typo in either file leaves the field null and the first click throws a NullPointerException.

## Check before running

- The controller class is public and has a public no argument constructor.
- Every `@FXML` field is private, matching the attribute name exactly.
- `onAction="#onSave"` matches a method, and the method takes no arguments or one ActionEvent.
- `initialize` is optional but must be annotated when used with FXML.
